heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S produces exceptional carbon-fiber composite parts up to 179 mm/s capped at a 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. However, printing Bambu PETG-CF requires upgrading the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears to hardened steel to prevent rapid abrasive wear.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with thin layer of glue stick or liquid release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap 'Max volumetric speed' at 15 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high travel velocities.
Set 'Pressure Advance' to approximately 0.038 s and run dynamic flow calibration via OrcaSlicer for clean seam alignment.
Reduce 'Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan' to 0% to prevent rapid differential cooling and edge warping on enclosed structural prints.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm to mitigate carbon fiber whisker stringing across open travels.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe bed tearing or permanent adhesion to PEI sheet
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG binds chemically to smooth PEI surfaces when printed hot without a barrier layer.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply Bambu Liquid Glue or a standard glue stick as a release agent on a Textured PEI Plate, and maintain bed temperature at 73°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder gear slipping or sudden partial nozzle clogging
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive chopped carbon fibers eroding the stock stainless steel nozzle orifice or lodging in worn extruder gear teeth.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Swap both the hotend assembly and extruder drive gears to Bambu Lab hardened steel components.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Fine filament hairs and fuzzy stringing between perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in PETG polymer matrix boiling out at 255°C nozzle temperatures.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in an active convection dryer at 65°C for at least 8 hours prior to printing from the AMS.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PETG-CF using the stock P1S nozzle?
faq.answer: No, the P1S comes standard with a stainless steel nozzle and extruder gear, which will quickly erode from the chopped carbon fibers; upgrade to Bambu hardened steel hardware before printing.

faq.question: Should I keep the P1S front door and top glass open during printing?
faq.answer: Keep the chamber closed to maintain thermal stability around 35-40°C, which prevents warping in PETG-CF, but keep auxiliary cooling fans off.

faq.question: Is Bambu PETG-CF compatible with the standard Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, Bambu PETG-CF is fully compatible with the AMS, provided the spool is dried and cardboard edges (if non-Bambu spools are used) are rimmed.

faq.question: What print speed cap should I specify in OrcaSlicer for PETG-CF?
faq.answer: Limit outer walls to 120-150 mm/s and infill up to 179 mm/s, regulated under a strict 15 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate.
